task.description: The page has a question block #faq (each .faq__item has a .faq__question button with aria-expanded="false" and a hidden answer .faq__answer), a #save-btn button and a hidden notification #toast with .toast__text and a .toast__close button. The platform has already turned off animations ($.fx.off = true) so that the tests see the result right away. 1) If window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches, turn off animations: $.fx.off = true (not allowed without the condition). 2) Accordion: with one delegated handler $("#faq").on("click", ".faq__question", ...), when a question is clicked, close the other answers with .slideUp() and set aria-expanded="false" on their buttons, and toggle this question's answer with .slideToggle() and write "true" or "false" to this button's aria-expanded. Take the state from aria-expanded, not from :visible. Questions added after the page loads must also work. 3) Write the function showToast(message): it writes message into .toast__text and shows #toast with .fadeIn(). 4) A click on #save-btn calls showToast("Settings saved"). 5) A click on .toast__close hides #toast with .fadeOut(). Handlers - only with .on(); do not use document.querySelector, innerHTML, .html(), .style or .click(fn).

questions.question: How is $("#box").hide() different from $("#box").fadeOut()?
options: hide() hides it at once, fadeOut() smoothly lowers the opacity and sets display: none at the end
hide() removes the element from the DOM
fadeOut() only makes the element transparent, but its space stays taken
questions.explanation: Both methods end up setting display: none, but fadeOut does it after a smooth change of opacity (400 ms by default).

questions.explanation: An animation does not stop the program: the next line runs right away, and the completion function is called after the effect ends.

questions.question: Which forms set the effect duration correctly?
questions.explanation: The duration is a number of milliseconds or the words "fast" (200) and "slow" (600). The string "300ms" is not recognized, and jQuery uses the default 400 ms.

questions.question: A user quickly clicked a button with $panel.slideToggle() 10 times. What happens?
options: The panel opens and closes 10 times in a row, even after the user has stopped clicking
The panel stays in the middle of the animation
questions.explanation: Each call joins the fx queue. The cure is .stop(true, true) before the effect.

questions.question: Match the code with the action.
pairs: Stop the current animation, the queue continues
Stop the current one and clear the queue
Clear the queue and jump to the end of the current animation
questions.explanation: The first argument of stop clears the queue, the second brings the current animation to its final state.

questions.question: Which property must be set to true to make all jQuery animations instant? Enter the whole expression, for example $.xxx.yyy
questions.explanation: $.fx.off = true - effects jump to their final state at once. This is how you respect the prefers-reduced-motion setting.

questions.question:
What does the code do?
if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches) { $.fx.off = true; }
options: Turns off animations on mobile devices
Turns off jQuery animations if "reduce motion" is on in the system
Turns animations on if the browser turned them off
questions.explanation: matchMedia checks a media query from JavaScript; .matches is true if the user asks for less motion.

questions.question: Which properties can you change smoothly with .animate() without plugins?
questions.explanation: .animate() works only with numeric properties. A color is not a number - it needs a plugin or a CSS transition.

questions.question: Why is it better to take the accordion state from aria-expanded rather than from $answer.is(":visible")?
options: During the closing animation the answer is still visible, and is(":visible") returns true
is() cannot be called in a handler
questions.explanation: While slideUp is running, the element is visible. The attribute changes at once and shows the intention, and screen readers also read it.

questions.question: Which method, in one call, shows a hidden block or hides a visible one by smoothly changing its height? Enter the method name without the dot and brackets.
questions.explanation: slideToggle chooses slideDown or slideUp based on the current state.

questions.question: Match the task with the best tool.
pairs: Open a menu on click, the animation is described in CSS
Smoothly expand a block of unknown height
Remove an element after it disappears
questions.explanation: Simple transitions belong in CSS, and JavaScript only toggles a class. jQuery is handy where you need auto height or an action after the animation.

questions.question:
What will the code print if the page has 3 .card elements?
$(".card").fadeOut(200, function () { console.log("done"); });
questions.explanation: The completion function is called separately for each element; this inside is the current element.
